capabilityIntro: Bring an approved route, a set of field records, or a defined redline backlog. We produce the drawings and schedules your OSP team needs, keep them synchronized, and flag questions for your reviewer before handoff.
buyerRoles: OSP design leads at broadband operators and cooperatives who need consistent route and construction documentation
Engineering prime project managers who need a defined work package with review boundaries and native file handoff
Fiber construction teams that need controlled drawing updates before the next review or field release

capabilities.title: HLD route and service-area production
capabilities.summary: Translate the buyer’s approved network architecture and route concept into consistent map and schedule records for review.
inputs: Approved route corridors, service-area limits, and architecture rules
Available basemap, structures, and service point data with capture dates
outputs: Route map and labeled endpoints or service areas
Length and structure counts by segment with assumptions
Log of missing route inputs or decisions
checks: Tie segment identifiers and endpoints between the map and schedule
Distinguish sourced geometry from geometry awaiting confirmation

capabilities.title: LLD aerial and underground plan sheets
capabilities.summary: Build coordinated plan sheets from approved route geometry and construction criteria. Maintain visible cross-references between sheets and details.
inputs: Route geometry, stationing conventions, and client drawing templates
Field records and controlled details for poles, ducts, handholes, or crossings
outputs: Plan sheets, key map, match lines, and referenced details
Sheet index, structure schedule, and reviewer exceptions
Native working files and a PDF review set in agreed versions
checks: Trace each detailed segment through the key map and matching sheet
Check for unresolved field conflicts and missing input references before packaging

capabilities.title: Splice schedules and material quantities
capabilities.summary: Tie cable IDs, fiber groups, closures, and quantities to the same design revision so reviewers can compare them with the drawings.
inputs: Approved cable sizes, fiber assignments, and splice rules
Measured route lengths, allocation assumptions, and required units
outputs: Cable and fiber-group schedule by splice enclosure
Material quantities split between measured length and allowances
Exceptions for unassigned fibers or unconfirmed units
checks: Trace each fiber group through its incoming and outgoing cable
Cross-check measured lengths, cable allowances, and unit labels against the plan

capabilities.title: Crossing and permit exhibit preparation
capabilities.summary: Compile the graphics and source crosswalk that the buyer’s reviewer needs to assess a proposed crossing and prepare their submission.
inputs: Owner-provided right-of-way limits and crossing exhibits
Stationed survey or utility records and the buyer’s approved detail criteria
outputs: Stationed crossing exhibit and referenced detail sheet
Requirements crosswalk with evidence references and assigned owners
Conflict register with a hold or decision request for unverified conditions
checks: Reconcile station limits and source references between exhibit and schedule
Carry unknown depths, utility conflicts, and permitting dependencies as open items

capabilities.title: Redline revisions and turnover coordination
capabilities.summary: Process consolidated markups and track each impacted drawing, data record, and schedule under a single revision.
inputs: Last controlled plan set and related schedule versions
Consolidated redlines with the approving reviewer and source for each instruction
outputs: Updated sheets, quantity deltas, and disposition of comments
Handoff index with current file versions and dependent records
Open-item and exclusion log for deferred decisions
checks: Track affected IDs, sheets, schedules, and counts before and after
Retain prior revision records alongside the dated handoff and exception log

formats: PDF review sets and native CAD records in agreed file versions
CSV or XLSX schedules with documented units, revision IDs, and field names
GeoPackage, shapefile, or KMZ exchange only when scoped and validated in the receiving workflow
requirements: Identify the controlled source set, its revision, and the authorized reviewer
Agree on the route limits, templates, intake channel, and receiving file formats
Record the acceptance criteria, review window, and how to handle open issues
boundaries: The designated reviewer controls design decisions, field certification, and sign-off
The buyer or authorized permitting party controls submissions and permit status
Use a controlled file exchange after confirming authority and data requirements

projects.title: Aerial distribution plans and splice continuity
projects.summary: A synthetic 1,315-foot route across four poles, with a two-sheet handoff, one splice closure, and matched cable quantities.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic aerial route schematic showing four poles, three spans, two drawing sheets, and splice closure SC-103 at the match point
projects.context: A fictional cooperative has selected one aerial segment for a production trial. Its design lead provides four pole IDs and three approved spans. The reviewing team needs the plan split, cable IDs, splice records, and allowance calculations to agree.
constraints: Four fictional poles and three fixed spans
Two sheets meeting at P-103 and closure SC-103
Two 48-fiber cables with a demonstration allowance of 20 feet per cable end

approach.title: Split the plan at a known structure
approach.text: Place the first two spans on A-101 and the final span on A-102. Use P-103 as the shared reference for the drawing and splice matrix.

approach.title: Trace cable and fiber groups
approach.text: Link cable C-101 to C-102 at SC-103. Carry active fibers 1–24 and reserved fibers 25–48 through matching groups on both sides.

approach.title: Separate placement footage and allowances
approach.text: Add 40 feet of illustrative end allowance per cable. Keep it separate so the buyer can revise the assumptions without changing surveyed route length.

deliverables: Two-sheet aerial route and match-line schematic
Span schedule keyed by pole, sheet, and cable ID
Fiber-group splice matrix and cable quantity schedule
verification: C-101 uses 945 route feet and C-102 uses 370 route feet. The 80-foot sample allowance brings the total to 1,395 feet
The splice matrix uses every fiber 1–48 exactly once on each cable
projects.review: Synthetic production example. The plan division and schedules demonstrate consistency. Pole loading, field clearance, and construction release are outside this sample.

files.label: Span and sheet schedule
files.description: Three spans with pole IDs, sheet references, route feet, and cable assignments.

files.label: 48-fiber splice matrix
files.description: Four fiber groups carried through closure SC-103 with active and reserved assignments.

files.label: Cable quantity schedule
files.description: Measured route feet, terminal allowances, and the resulting scheduled footage by cable.

projects.title: Underground road crossing review package
projects.summary: A synthetic 340-foot crossing segment with a 240-foot proposed bore and a clearly marked utility-depth decision.
projects.imageAlt: Fictional road crossing exhibit showing bore stations 0+35 to 2+75 and a utility depth hold at station 1+43
projects.context: A fictional municipality’s reviewer needs a crossing exhibit and requirements register. The proposed bore is stationed from 0+35 to 2+75. A utility crossing at 1+43 has an unverified depth in the source records.
constraints: All stations and constraints are fictional
The vertical profile is schematic and does not establish depths or clearances
The unverified utility depth stays open for field confirmation and reviewer disposition

approach.title: Assign a single station reference
approach.text: Record both approaches and the bore against the same baseline and use it for the exhibit and conflict register.

approach.title: Identify what the reviewer needs
approach.text: Cross-reference the right-of-way sketch, utility locate note, and owner’s detail reference against the open requirements.

approach.title: Keep the hold visible
approach.text: Attach the missing utility-depth confirmation to station 1+43. Assign field verification and route disposition to their respective owners.

deliverables: Stationed crossing graphic with proposed limits and the unresolved utility conflict
Segment schedule for the approaches and bore
Requirements crosswalk with evidence and ownership
verification: Approaches of 35 and 65 feet plus a 240-foot bore total 340 feet
The proposed bore lies between 0+35 and 2+75 and spans the fictional roadway from 1+04 to 1+56
Station 1+43 and the open utility-depth hold match between exhibit and crosswalk
projects.review: Synthetic exhibit preparation example. The authorized reviewer and governing agency control any clearance, construction, or permitting decision.

files.label: Crossing station schedule
files.description: Approach and bore limits, roadway reference, and the unresolved utility point.

files.label: Requirements and conflict crosswalk
files.description: Evidence and responsibility for the fictional ROW sketch, utility conflict, and detail reference.

projects.title: Handhole relocation and quantity reconciliation
projects.summary: A synthetic field redline moves a handhole 15 feet. The revision shows the transfer between two cable spans and carries one open locator discrepancy forward.
projects.imageAlt: Before and after diagrams showing handhole HH-04 moving from station 8+07 to 8+22 while total route length stays 780 feet
projects.context: A fictional construction team submits redline RL-01 to shift a handhole on an existing corridor. Two cable records reference the handhole. The reviewer needs the sheet and schedule differences, fiber continuity, and remaining open issue in one place.
constraints: The corridor endpoints are fixed at stations 2+25 and 10+05
The controlled redline covers a 15-foot handhole move and no other design change
The locator discrepancy at the downstream marker remains open

approach.title: Retain a prior revision reference
approach.text: Compare sheet UG-204 at R00 and R01. Move HH-04 from station 8+07 to 8+22 while retaining its structure ID.

approach.title: Update dependent records together
approach.text: Extend C-201 by 15 feet and shorten C-202 by 15 feet. Record that the 48-fiber groups retain their prior assignments.

approach.title: Separate the remaining issue
approach.text: Log the locator-marker discrepancy as RL-02 with a field follow-up owner and carry it in the handoff as an unresolved record.

deliverables: Cable and splice change schedule with prior and current values
verification: HH-04 keeps its asset ID and fiber assignments across both revisions
projects.review: Synthetic revision example. The resulting package is prepared for buyer review. The drawing release and field asset reconciliation require the designated reviewer.

files.label: Cable and splice delta schedule
files.description: Before and after measurements and 48-fiber assignments keyed to UG-204.

files.label: Redline and exception register
files.description: Revision trace for the handhole move and the still-open downstream marker issue.
